summary: Round-2 production hardening validation for La Maison d'Auben in Stripe TEST mode. Extended pytest suite from 46 → 52 tests, all 52 PASS in ~35s. Added 6 new tests covering the 5 fixes: (FIX1) origin_url/CORS hardening — POST /api/payments/checkout with hostile body origin_url='https://evil-hacker.example.com' returns 200 with a cs_test_ session on checkout.stripe.com; server-side retrieval of the Stripe session (via test secret key) confirms success_url starts with the preview PUBLIC_BASE_URL and contains '/paiement/succes?session_id=…' while cancel_url ends with '/paiement/annule' — the hostile domain appears NOWHERE in success_url or cancel_url. Normal-origin checkout still returns cs_test_ session. (FIX4) atomic download limit — reset a paid order's counter to 0 and limit to 5 via Mongo, fired 30 concurrent GET /api/download/{token} with a ThreadPoolExecutor(20): exactly ≤5 responses were 200, the remaining 25 returned 429, download_count in DB matched the number of 200s and never exceeded 5; one extra call after saturation returned 429. State restored (count=0, limit=25) for downstream tests. (FIX5) email retry/recovery — POST /api/admin/orders/{id}/resend-email returns 200 and does not duplicate the order; separate email_status and owner_email_status fields remain distinct; 404 on unknown order id; forced 'sending' state with a 10-min-old email_status_at was successfully reclaimed on retry (post-call status ∈ {sent,failed,skipped,pending} or 'sending' with a fresh timestamp — never stuck on stale sending). (FIX2) admin auth continues to work using ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD read from env (falls back to /app/backend/.env with an assertion — no hardcoded secrets). CORE REGRESSION intact: happy path (checkout→pay→by-session→download xlsx ~1MB attachment Budget-mensuel.xlsx 7.99 EUR); unpaid session ⇒ no order & by-session 404 & payment_status≠paid; idempotency (repeated + 10 concurrent by-session → exactly 1 order); admin endpoints require Bearer (401 without); rate limiting (admin_login 429 after 5, contact after 5, newsletter after 10, checkout after 20; per X-Forwarded-For IP); upload validation (.txt/.exe/empty → 400, .png → 200); products=6 incl 'Suivi sportif'; categories=8 with 'sport' & no 'investissement'; settings/articles(3)/faq 200; boot log 'Stripe initialisé | mode=test | cle=test' present.

minor.issue: Customer confirmation emails to arbitrary gmail.com recipients still return 422 (recipient allowlist) → email_status='failed'. Order & endpoint behave correctly (200, no duplication, stale-sending recovery works). Will resolve behind production Resend domain.

critical_code_review_comments: FIX1 verified at Stripe API level: create_checkout hard-codes success_url/cancel_url from PUBLIC_BASE_URL and ignores req.origin_url. Retrieving the created Session via stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve confirmed no client-supplied host appears in success_url/cancel_url. origin_url is kept in CheckoutInput only for backward compatibility of the request schema — recommend removing it entirely from CheckoutInput and updating the frontend so that hostile clients cannot even set the field (defense-in-depth; not a blocker).

FIX4 atomic guard is correct: db.orders.update_one({'download_token':tok,'download_count':{'$lt':limit}}, {'$inc':{'download_count':1}}) is fully atomic in MongoDB; modified_count==0 ⇒ 429. Refund on storage read failure via $inc:-1 restores fairness. Under 30-way concurrency, count never exceeded configured limit.

FIX5 _claim_email correctly matches {field ∈ ['pending','failed']} OR {field=='sending' AND at<stale} OR {field=='sending' AND at missing}. The resend endpoint takes a shortcut by force-resetting email_status='pending' before calling _send_customer_email — this always triggers a retry regardless of stale-detection. That is acceptable but means the '>5 min sending recovery' path is exercised by the automatic retry loop (e.g. webhook re-arriving during a crashed prior send), not by resend-email. Consider also exposing owner_email_status resend, and adding a small admin endpoint to retry only stale-sending owner emails without resetting to 'pending'.

FIX2: tests now read ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD from os.environ with a fallback loader that parses /app/backend/.env at import time — no secrets are hardcoded in the test source. Consider using python-dotenv for cleaner semantics, and refuse to run if env is missing (already asserted).
Rate limiter remains in-memory per process — still a caveat behind multi-worker deployments; unchanged from previous review.
test_credentials: ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD read from env or /app/backend/.env (not hardcoded). Stripe TEST card 4242 4242 4242 4242.
seed_data_creation: No new real Stripe purchase performed this iteration — reused the paid Budget-mensuel order seeded in iteration_5 (cs_test_a1FME0h…). New tests created several extra unpaid cs_test_ sessions (checkout with hostile origin, normal origin, extra-fields overrides) — none produced orders (verified).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite now has 52 tests. New groups: TestOriginUrlHardening (FIX1: hostile origin_url ignored, deep server-side check via Stripe API using the test secret key from backend/.env), TestAtomicDownloadLimit (FIX4: 30-way concurrency against /api/download/{tok} with limit temporarily reset to 5 via Mongo, verifying count≤limit and remaining 429s; state restored to count=0/limit=25 for downstream tests), TestEmailRetryAndRecovery (FIX5: resend-email no duplication, 404 on unknown id, stale-sending recovery by manually setting email_status='sending' with 10-min-old email_status_at and asserting the value is reclaimed). Tests use motor+asyncio.run() for direct Mongo manipulation; MONGO_URL/DB_NAME loaded from backend/.env. If you need to trigger another real purchase to refresh the paid order fixture, follow iteration_5 context_for_next_testing_agent guidance. Rate-limit tests still isolate by X-Forwarded-For IPs 203.0.113.11..14 — reuse those or pick different values.
rca of the issue: N/A — all 5 fixes verified. Only intermittent case is the earlier state-leak between the atomic-limit test and test_download_endpoint_on_latest_order (fixed inside the new test by restoring download_count/download_limit after the concurrency check).
